items.q: So, Jo Jones never forgot that. We always knew each other from that for

ctx.x: He was playing there. Well, he was playing in a band there with J.T. Watley. So, I asked him to let me play, sit down and play in his place. I had a little nerve, you know. Now, on them drums he was playing, I want to sit down in a big band. That's where I first had a contact to sit in a big band and play. So, Jo Jones never forgot that. items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: when you look up and see Erskine, Erskine would be on trumpet and I would be on trumpet.

ctx.x: Did you ever play with Erskine Hawkins' band?

Of course not, because when you look up and see Erskine, Erskine would be on trumpet and I would be on trumpet. Until 1930 I was playing the second part to 'Beau Koo Jack.' Of course I had to put a Coca-Cola bottle... 'Beau Koo Jack' in the key of B flat. Mr. Don Redman (HUMS) - that's on the second page and you paid 50¢ for that stack. That was a big stack. 'Beau Koo Jack' and 'Louisiana Bobo.' See I played all those things... But my embouchure went away because at the same time I had met a fellow by the name of…
